subject: dragonfly larva
title: Baby Dragonflies Breathe Through Their Rear and Fire Their Jaw at Fish

scenes.text: Before it can fly, a dragonfly spends years underwater. Breathing through its rear.
The larva pumps water in and out of its rectum, where its gills are hidden. Some species live like this for up to five years.
Squeeze that water out hard, and the larva shoots forward like a jet. That is its getaway and its attack.
Its lower jaw is folded under its head like an arm. When a tadpole drifts close, the jaw unfolds and grabs in about 60 milliseconds.
Faster than you blink. Tadpoles, mosquito larvae, even small fish get pulled back to the mouth.
Then one day it crawls out of the water, splits its skin, and the jet-powered killer becomes a dragonfly.

description:
Dragonfly larvae live underwater for months to years before they ever fly, and some species spend up to five years as nymphs. Their gills sit inside the rectum: they breathe by pumping water in and out, and by expelling it hard they jet forward.
Their hinged lower jaw folds under the head and shoots out to grab prey; high-speed video in a 2021 study measured the extension at roughly 60 milliseconds, faster than a human blink. They eat mosquito larvae, tadpoles and small fish.
Did you know the dragonfly in your garden spent years as this? Comment below.
first_comment: The larva's jaw is driven partly by water pressure from the same system it breathes with, so the breath and the strike share one engine. Which animal baby is scarier than the adult? Comment below.
